newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire to lift exchange controls soon - employers.
newsitem.headline: Zaire to lift exchange controls soon - employers.

text.p: Zaire's central bank will soon abandon controls on foreign exchange flows, the country's influential Employers' Association said on Tuesday.

"The repatriation of export receipts will be achieved through commercial banks, and exporters will no longer have to retrocede receipts to the central bank," Luboya Diyoka, the association's administrator told Reuters in an interview.
Luboya, who is on the central bank committee which is discussing the changes, did not specify when the controls would be lifted but said it would be "very soon".
"Direct capital movements will be freed and can pass by any commercial bank, as can payments for imports," he said.

The western-backed government of Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo has been trying to implement economic reforms aimed at liberalising markets and increasing foreign investment in the mineral-rich country.
Since Kengo took office in 1994 annual inflation has been reduced from four digits to three and efforts have been made to reform corrupt and inefficient state enterprises and cut government spending.
Zaire has the mineral and agricultural resources to make it one of Africa's richest nations, but is in a state of advanced decline after years of mismanagement and political crisis.
The latest crisis erupted in the refugee-swamped east, where the army has been pushed back from the eastern frontier by Rwandan-backed Tutsi rebels.
